claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on a narrow aggregate-readiness basis despite an unresolved disclosure question for the mortgage servicing assistant segment.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation was disclosed or that approved risk acceptance exists.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A launch-ready disclosure artifact or a documented approved risk acceptance referencing this limitation and use case.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy expressly requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before launch for material limitations affecting named launch use cases.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies on low projected traffic to argue non-materiality despite evidence that the segment is named in two servicer pilot commitments.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence that the commitments were removed, are not launch commitments, or otherwise do not make the segment a named launch use case.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy text says low-volume labeling does not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review remains open on whether the gap must be disclosed.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A final legal determination or equivalent admissible closure showing disclosure is not required or has been satisfied.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Pending legal review is explicitly part of the policy context that prevents product characterization alone from resolving materiality.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor uses aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents as support for certification even though those facts do not answer the disclosure requirement.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Evidence directly addressing the disclosure predicate rather than general readiness metrics.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: These facts may support operational readiness but do not satisfy the specific policy condition governing material limitation disclosure.

decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
For named launch use cases, material limitations must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Evidence tied only to aggregate readiness cannot cure a missing disclosure or approval predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide admissible evidence that the material limitation was disclosed in the model card or equivalent launch disclosure.
Provide admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case before launch.
Provide the final legal determination on whether the mortgage servicing assistant gap must be disclosed.
Provide evidence that the named servicer pilot commitments were amended, deferred, or otherwise no longer make this a named launch use case.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting a named launch use case unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The affected mortgage servicing assistant segment is a named launch use case and is tied to two servicer pilot commitments, which makes the limitation material under the provided policy text.
Legal review is still open, so materiality and disclosure have not been resolved.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance or a completed disclosure plan that would satisfy the release policy.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents speak to launch viability, not to compliance with the disclosure requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is supportable on the present record under the release policy.
That low projected first-month traffic is a sufficient basis to omit a material weakness disclosure.
That public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring can substitute for the specific internal policy predicate requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
